skill.name: arch-tech-evaluation
skill.description: Evaluates technology options across requirements, performance, reliability, operations, cost, ecosystem, and team readiness, then produces a recommendation and proof-of-concept plan.
skill.summary: Compare technology candidates, expose tradeoffs, and produce a structured recommendation with validation steps.
skill.author: zl2023github

content.user_title: Evaluate Technology Choices with Clear Tradeoffs
content.value_statement: Technology choices often hide tradeoffs across performance, cost, reliability, operations, and team readiness. This skill compares candidates, recommends an option, and defines proof-of-concept checks.
actual_capabilities: Clarifies business goals, system scale, team skills, and nonfunctional constraints.
Compares two or more technologies across weighted technical and operational dimensions.
Documents strengths, tradeoffs, recommendation reasons, and mitigation actions.
Designs proof-of-concept checks for throughput, latency, reliability, and recovery.
Produces a structured Markdown evaluation report and an optional architecture decision record.
limitations: Recommendations depend on accurate constraints and current product information supplied by the user.
The skill does not run benchmarks, deploy candidates, or verify vendor claims.
Default weights are general guidance and require adjustment for each organization.
Cost, licensing, security, and community data can become outdated and need independent validation.

use_cases.title: Select Messaging Infrastructure
use_cases.description: Compare message brokers against throughput, latency, durability, recovery, ecosystem, and operating requirements.

use_cases.title: Choose an Application Framework
use_cases.description: Evaluate frameworks against delivery needs, team experience, maintenance effort, security, and total cost.

use_cases.title: Plan a Defensible Decision
use_cases.description: Define proof-of-concept tests and record the final choice, evidence, risks, and rejected alternatives.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Two Options
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare [option A] and [option B] for [use case]. Focus on functionality, performance, cost, operations, and learning curve. Recommend one option.
prompt_templates.scenario: Begin with a direct comparison when requirements are simple.

prompt_templates.title: Evaluate Against Constraints
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate [candidates] for [system]. Use these constraints: [scale], [latency], [availability], [consistency], [budget], and [team experience]. Create a weighted comparison and identify missing information.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use measurable requirements to produce a more specific recommendation.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Proof of Concept
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a proof of concept for choosing among [candidates]. Define hypotheses, workloads, metrics, pass criteria, failure tests, effort, and decision rules.
prompt_templates.scenario: Validate the assumptions that could change the selection.

prompt_templates.title: Produce an Architecture Decision
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess [candidates] for [architecture]. Build a weighted scorecard, sensitivity analysis, risk register, migration plan, and final recommendation. Draft an ADR that records rejected alternatives and evidence gaps.
prompt_templates.scenario: Create a reviewable decision package for a high-impact architecture choice.

output_examples.input: Compare Kafka and RabbitMQ for order events at 100,000 messages per second.
output_examples.output: **Recommendation: Kafka.** It better matches sustained throughput and retention needs. Validate p99 latency, broker recovery, consumer rebalancing, and operational capacity in a proof of concept.

output_examples.input: Choose between two web frameworks for a small team maintaining a business application.
output_examples.output: **Recommendation: Framework A.** Its team familiarity and simpler operations outweigh Framework B's performance advantage. Reassess when traffic or real-time requirements increase.

output_examples.input: Create a proof-of-concept plan and ADR for selecting a distributed database.
output_examples.output: The plan measures latency, failover, consistency, recovery, and cost under representative workloads. The ADR records weighted scores, unresolved risks, and the approval criteria.

best_practices: Provide measurable workload, latency, availability, consistency, retention, budget, and compliance constraints.
Adjust dimension weights with stakeholders before scoring candidates.
Validate decisive assumptions with benchmarks, documentation, and a time-boxed proof of concept.
anti_patterns: Do not select a technology from popularity or star counts alone.
Do not treat default scores as universal facts across teams and workloads.
Do not finalize a recommendation while critical requirements or evidence remain unknown.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the use case, candidate technologies, scale, reliability targets, budget, timeline, team experience, existing stack, and compliance constraints.

faq.question: Can it evaluate any technology category?
faq.answer: Yes. The general workflow applies broadly, but evaluation dimensions and weights should match the specific technology category.

faq.question: Does it perform live benchmarks?
faq.answer: No. It designs benchmark and proof-of-concept plans, but users must run the tests and supply measured results.

faq.question: How are recommendations calculated?
faq.answer: Candidates are compared across weighted dimensions. The final recommendation also considers tradeoffs, risks, missing evidence, and organizational constraints.

faq.question: Can it create an architecture decision record?
faq.answer: Yes. It can format the selected option, decision context, evidence, consequences, risks, and rejected alternatives as an ADR.

faq.question: How should I handle outdated facts?
faq.answer: Verify product versions, pricing, licenses, security history, and community activity with current primary sources before approving the decision.
